question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(3,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\sum }_{{x}_{i}\le x}{\sum }_{{y}_{i}\le y}f({x}_{i},{y}_{i}).
$$

By definition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(3,-1) & =P(X\le 3,Y\le -1).\end{aligned}
$$

We start by highlighting all cells in the table that correspond to $X\le 3,Y\le -1.$

| $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}F(3,-1) & ={\sum }_{x\le 3}{\sum }_{y\le -1}f(x,y) \\  & =f(1,-1)+f(2,-1)+f(3,-1) \\  & =0.1+0.05+0.05 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$
